subject: Very low alpha values suppress visibility  in Legend

messages.author: 519455d3bf64680d
messages.subject: Very low alpha values suppress visibility  in Legend
parts:
In plotting a large dataset (n=500K) I have used very low alpha levels
(a=0.02). This yields a lovely graph, with one exception... I can't see
the symbol/colour objects within the legend. The values ("Male" and
"Female") are there, of course, but the alpha value applies to both the
plot area and to the legend.

Compare:

library(diamonds)

ggplot(data=diamonds)+geom_point(aes(x=clarity, y=price, color=colour))


ggplot(data=diamonds)+geom_point(aes(x=clarity, y=price,
color=color),alpha=0.1)

and note the vividness of the colours in legend is noticeably reduced.

I've subsequently facetted on the colour-term variable (sex), but it
would be nice to retain the colour in addition to the facetting.

Should alpha apply to the legend?

Any suggestions?

messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f

On Fri, Jun 3, 2011 at 21:49, Rob James <r...@aetiologic.ca> wrote:
> In plotting a large dataset (n=500K) I have used very low alpha levels
> (a=0.02). This yields a lovely graph, with  one exception... I can't see the
> symbol/colour objects within the legend.  The values ("Male" and "Female")
> are there, of course, but the alpha value applies to both the plot area and
> to the legend.
>
> Compare:
>
> library(diamonds)
>
> ggplot(data=diamonds)+geom_point(aes(x=clarity, y=price, color=colour))
>
> ggplot(data=diamonds)+geom_point(aes(x=clarity, y=price,
> color=color),alpha=0.1)

A bit of a hack but this should work:

ggplot(data=diamonds)+geom_point(aes(x=clarity, y=price, color=color,
alpha=0)) + scale_alpha(to=c(0.1,0.1), legend=FALSE)

what you do is:
- map alpha to a constant (1 here)
- since alpha is mapped, you can modify its scale. Use the range to
which the transparency is scaled in scale_alpha to set the actual
transparency ("to" argument; 0.1 here, 0.02 for you)
- do not display alpha scaling in the legend (legend=FALSE)

JiHO
